newsitem.title: USA: Russia tells Clinton Yeltsin operation successful.
newsitem.headline: Russia tells Clinton Yeltsin operation successful.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin telephoned President Bill Clinton on Tuesday and told him President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery had been successful, U.S. officials said.

Chernomyrdin telephoned Clinton here on Election Day to report on the success of the operation performed on Tuesday, a White House official travelling with Clinton said, adding that the conversation was brief.
In Washington, Defence Department spokesman Ken Bacon said the United States was not concerned about the security of Russia's nuclear weapons while the operation was underway.
"We believe that adequate steps were taken to oversee and command the nuclear arsenal by turning over government authority to Prime Minister Chernomyrdin," Bacon said.
The State Department said Washington was pleased Yeltsin's heart operation appeared to go well and officials said they hoped to get a private briefing from one of his doctors.

"The United States is very pleased that President Yeltsin's operation appears to have gone well and we wish him the best for a speedy and full recovery," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters. "We look forward to the day when he can resume fully his responsibilities as president of Russia."
Chernomyrdin will hold the reins of power during Yeltsin's convalescence and Burns said "we have an excellent relationship with Prime Minister Chernomyrdin and have full confidence in him."

Officials said privately they were trying to get a briefing on Yeltsin's condition from Michael DeBakey, 88. The pioneering American surgeon, an observer at the surgery, said in Moscow: "The operation was a complete success."

Yeltsin came through seven hours of open-heart surgery but it will be some time before Russians will know if the 65-year-old president can return to full health and stamp his authority on the Kremlin.
